headline: Recommended selling CNG fueling equipment and recycling trucks, trucks to Casella at appraised value; sent proposed recycling ordinance to council for first reading.
summary: Heard a GMT study on microtransit and ADA service, with no action taken. Sent a proposed ordinance requiring curbside recycling residents to use the city's consolidated recycling service to council for first reading. Recommended selling CNG equipment and recycling trucks.
decisions: Sent the draft residential recycling collection ordinance to council for first reading and referral to the ordinance committee, unanimous.
Recommended that the Board of Finance and City Council approve sale of CNG equipment and the recycling fleet to Casella at appraised value, unanimous.

1. Agenda

Councilor Broderick seconds. 
All in favor, Unanimous approval   
 
2. Minutes of 9/29/26 
Councilor Bergman moves to adopt the minutes as posted. 
Councilor Broderick seconds.  
All in favor, Unanimous approval 
 
3. Public Forum 
Andrea from Heineburg Senior Center – interested in what is going on with Micro transit and 
ADA. 
 
4. Deliberative Agenda 
 4.1 GMT Micro mobility & ADA Study 
Chris Damiani, Director of Planning for GMT & Clayton Clark General Manager of GMT 
presented information. 
 
Councilor Bergman asked if the study has all of the details?  Did the study look into a 
Burlington only pilot?  Councilor Broderick thinks for Burlington you would want Microtransit 
to enhance the service that we already have. Councilor McKnight thinks its great. Feels like 
we are stuck because of funding cuts and not hearing a lot of encouragement and increase in 
usage of public transport. Chair Barlow has questions around how if fits in the current eco
system?  The ¾ mile outside of existing service – places out of ¾ mile- they would call for 
mobility ride?  
 
Public Comments - Andrea stated that companies that specifically develop software for this 
doesn’t seem that SSTA has that.  Is there a way to improve SSTA?  Access to the hospital 
and Tilley Drive is a struggle for residents.  
  
AI generated minutes w/ slight staff revisions: Chris Damiani and Clayton Clark from Green 
Mountain Transit presented a study on microtransit implementation in Chittenden County, 
explaining that GMT was the first transit agency to implement microtransit in Vermont's 
Montpelier-Berlin area starting in 2021. The study goals focused on efficiently serving ADA and 
older adult passengers while enhancing fixed route service, with an estimated 230,000 annual 
passengers using the service within a 3/4-mile radius of existing fixed routes. The team noted 
significant cost differences between microtransit ($30-35 per passenger) and fixed route 
service ($6-7 per passenger), and highlighted that approximately 50-60% of microtransit rides 
would also involve fixed route service.  GMT discussed the potential implementation of 
microtransit services in Burlington, focusing on underserved timeframes such as early morning 
and late evening hours around the airport. The discussion highlighted the need for designated 
transfer points and coordination with the office of City Planning's mobility hub guidebook. GMT 
emphasized starting with small pilots to gather data and potentially scale up based on demand, 
while also exploring service agreements with non-municipal actors to align financials with 
beneficiaries. 
 
4.2 Draft Policy on Residential Recycling Collection 
Lee Perry, Division Director Maintenance Division provided information. 
 
Councilor Broderick asked if this was all that needs to be changed?  Do any changes or 
updates need to be made for enforcement?  Councilor Bergman doesn’t see its necessary to 
have a registration for those who self-haul.  Are we creating a system that needs to be 
created?  Councilor McKnight had some of the same questions as Councilor Broderick & 
Bergman.  This sounds good to her. Chair Barlow asked who is impacted by this? Supports 
this. 
  
AI generated minutes w/ slight staff revisions:  Lee Perry presented a proposed ordinance 
requiring residents who receive curbside recycling collection through toter to use the city's 
consolidated recycling service, aimed at addressing a $130,000 budget gap caused by 
decreased participation in the program. The discussion highlighted concerns about 
enforcement and potential loopholes, particularly around dumpster service for recycling.  The 
meeting focused on discussing a proposed solid waste generation tax ordinance. The group 
agreed to move forward with bringing the ordinance to the council for first reading on 
November 9th, with the motion including a requirement to conduct outreach to impacted 
property owners and haulers before the full council vote. 
Councilor Bergman moves to send this to the council for the next meeting for first reading 
and for referral to the ordinance committee and also include the request that DPW in the 
meantime to do the outreach to the people who are going to be brought in under this regime 
(new change) and do that engagement.  That engagement should include this as being sent to 
the full council for first reading and referral to the ordinance committee.
Councilor Broderick seconds.  
All in favor, Unanimous approval 
 
4.3 Possible Decommissioning of CNG Fueling Station 
Lee Perry, Division Director Maintenance Division provided information. 
 
Councilor Bergman is in support of making this happen. Asked how od recycling trucks are? 
Councilor Broderick said it makes sense to him.  Chair Barlow asked about the timing of the 
auction? 
AI generated minutes w/ slight staff revisions The discussion also began addressing a 
CNG refueling facility at 645 Pine Street that has been operating since 2007, though the 
details about its future were not fully covered in the transcript.  The committee discussed the 
decommissioning of the CNG facility and recycling trucks due to high maintenance costs and 
limited usage. They approved a motion to recommend the sale of CNG equipment and 
recycling trucks through public auction or scrap at fair market value.  
Councilor Bergman made the motion that recommends the Board of Finance and City 
Council to 1) approve the sale of the Compressed Natural Gas equipment associated with the 
refueling facility and any remaining equipment not purchased through auction will be sold as 
metal recycling at the current market price, and 2) approve the sale of the recycling fleet to 
Casella at appraised value, and any remaining truck not purchased be auctioned through any 
of the various online public auctions or, if the vehicle is of no value, Fleet Maintenance will 
have the recycling truck hauled away for scrap at the current market price.  
Councilor Broderick seconds. 
 All in favor, Unanimous approval
